newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek construction firm Etane goes public June 2-4.
newsitem.headline: Greek construction firm Etane goes public June 2-4.

text.p: Greek construction firm Etane SA is going public at 1,850 drachmas a share and will be a new listing on the Athens bourse's small-cap parallel market. Subscriptions to its initial public offering begin June 2-4.

Etane will tap the market for 777 million drachmas with an issue of 400,000 common registered shares with a par value of 100 drachmas. A 20,000 tranche will be privately placed with staff, also at 1,850 drachmas a share.

Lead underwriter and advisor to the issue is Telesis Securities with NIBID, Piraeus Bank, Xiosbank, Societe Generale-Athens, Ionian Bank, Egnatia Bank, European Popular Bank and Sarros Securities acting as co-underwriters to the issue.
Etane specialises in prefabricated construction, renovation and rehabilitation of landmark buildings and is a member of Europe's 500 -- an association of the fastest-growing European companies.
Its after-tax profits rose 65.4 percent to 402 million drachmas in fiscal 1996 on turnover growth of 28.5 percent -- 2.294 billion.
The company will use IPO proceeds to finance equipment acquisitions, boost working capital and retire debt.

Projections for this year see turnover rising to 3.1 billion drachmas with pretax earnings growing to 633 million. On an after-tax basis Etane is coming to market at a price earnings (P/E) ratio of 8.7 -- 8.3 times forecast 1997 net earnings.
"Etane is highly specialised in rehabilitation works, 30 percent of turnover, prefabricated construction, 50 percent, and construction management," said issue advisor Telesis Securities.

From an investment point of view it is not dependent on public sector construction and on average carries out a large number of projects -- 60-70 annually -- which reduces risk. Due to its expertise in complicated rehabilitation projects it enjoys higher profit margins.

"Etane is called upon to deliver fast construction projects as in the case of earthquake damages. Its industrial unit which puts out prefabricated units is a key factor which allows fast completion times," Telesis said in a company report.
The company has been present in Albania since 1993 and is now starting activities in Bosnia.
Etane has an orderbook of yet uncompleted projects worth 4.0 billion drachmas.

It is presently carrying out a feasibility study for the industrial production of 300 prefabricated homes using concrete in Bosnia. It is part of the Bosnian government's plan to relieve housing needs using prefabricated homes.
